consumer: The 'has any monster noticed the avatar' flag — the engine question 'is this monster aware of / tracking the avatar right now?', a yes/no the engine computes per nearby monster (not the tile-render panel, which is the non-load-bearing display half).
scope: Per nearby monster's tracked awareness of the avatar (its stored noticed/seen/hostile-tracking state), NOT a momentary geometric line-of-sight recompute — Creature::sees has the wrong reach for 'noticed'.
decisive_source: src/creature.cpp::Creature::sees — its body computes instantaneous can-see-right-now from range, light, LOS and concealment, returning a bool; an engine-computed predicate (so C-shaped), but its scope is current visibility, not persisted awareness, so it is the wrong-reach authority for 'has noticed'.
divergence: A monster that has already noticed the avatar and is actively pursuing it loses line of sight when the avatar steps behind a wall: Creature::sees returns false this turn, so a flag derived from sees() reads 'unnoticed', yet the monster is still hunting — the correct 'noticed' authority would read true.
